AS A RESULT OF THE COVID-19 VIRUS, AND RESULTING ORDERS AND DIRECTION FROM THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES, THE GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, AND THE ORANGE COUNTY HEALTH CARE AGENCY, AS WELL AS THE CITY OF IRVINE EMERGENCY DECLARATION, THE PUBLIC WILL NOT BE PERMITTED TO PHYSICALLY ATTEND THE IRVINE CITY COUNCIL MEETING TO WHICH THIS AGENDA APPLIES.
YOU MAY SUBMIT COMMENTS ON ANY AGENDA ITEM OR ON ANY ITEM NOT ON THE AGENDA, IN WRITING VIA MAIL TO “ATTN: CITY COUNCIL,” ONE CIVIC CENTER PLAZA, IRVINE, CA 92606; BY EMAIL TO CLERK@CITYOFIRVINE.ORG; OR THROUGH E-COMMENT AT CITYOFIRVINE.ORG/ICTV. YOU MAY WATCH THE MEETING LIVE ON ICTV, COX COMMUNICATIONS LOCAL ACCESS CHANNEL 30, AND AT&T U-VERSE CHANNEL 99, AND LIVESTREAMED ONLINE AT CITYOFIRVINE.ORG/ICTV.
PLEASE NOTE: THE CITY COUNCIL IS MAKING EVERY EFFORT TO FOLLOW THE SPIRIT AND INTENT OF THE BROWN ACT AND OTHER APPLICABLE LAWS REGULATING THE CONDUCT OF PUBLIC MEETINGS, IN ORDER TO MAXIMIZE TRANSPARENCY AND PUBLIC ACCESS. IT WOULD BE APPRECIATED IF COMMUNICATIONS OF PUBLIC COMMENTS RELATED TO ITEMS ON THE AGENDA, OR ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA, ARE PROVIDED PRIOR TO THE COMMENCEMENT OF THE MEETING. IF THAT IS NOT POSSIBLE, EVERY EFFORT WILL BE MADE TO ATTEMPT TO REVIEW E-COMMENTS DURING THE COURSE OF THE MEETING. TOWARDS THIS END, THE MAYOR WILL ENDEAVOR TO TAKE A BRIEF PAUSE BEFORE ACTION IS TAKEN ON ANY AGENDA ITEM TO ALLOW THE CITY CLERK TO REVIEW E-COMMENTS, AND SHARE ANY E-COMMENTS RECEIVED DURING THE MEETING.

LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 10 a.m. until the next City Council meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the City's ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv . For more information, please contact the City Clerk''s office at (949) 724-6205.
ADJOURNMENT
At 11:00 p.m., the City Council will determine which of the remaining agenda items can be considered and acted upon prior to 12:00 midnight and will continue all other items on which additional time is required until a future City Council meeting. All meetings are scheduled to terminate at 12:00 midnight.
STAFF REPORTS
As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are on file with the City Clerk and are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 12 days prior to a regular City Council meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org at least 12 days prior to the scheduled City Council meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv .
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL RECEIVED AFTER THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA
Any supplemental writings or documents distributed to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after the posting of the agenda will be available for public review in the City Clerk''s Office, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California, during normal business hours. In addition, such writings or documents will be made available for public review at the respective public meeting.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.

Media Types and Guidelines
Written Materials/Handouts:
Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to the meeting. This information will be disseminated to the City Council.
CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.
MEETING SCHEDULE

MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  October 27, 2020
  City Council Chamber
  One Civic Center Plaza
  Irvine, CA 92606

CALL TO ORDER
The regular meeting of the Irvine City Council was called to order at 4:32 p.m. on October
27, 2020, in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic Center, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine,
California; Mayor Shea presiding.
ROLL CALL
  Present:  5  Councilmember:  Melissa Fox
  Councilmember:  Farrah N. Khan
  Councilmember:  Anthony Kuo
  Vice Mayor:  Mike Carroll
  Mayor:  Christina Shea

Mayor Shea announced that the meeting was broadcast live on Cox Communications Local
Access Channel 30 and AT&T U-Verse Channel 99, and livestreamed online at
cityofirvine.org; and that in an effort to protect public health and prevent the spread of
COVID-19, the e-comment feature had been extended for all agenda items, which allowed
members of the public the ability to submit e-comments through the public comment portion
of each item and would be included as part of the official record and uploaded to the City’s
website. She also assured the community that the City of Irvine was adhering to the
Governor’s Executive Order in the Council Chamber and throughout City Hall by sanitizing
surfaces and equipment, as well as wearing face masks.
 City Council Minutes  October 27, 2020

  She also reiterated that general public comments on items not on the agenda would be
  considered at approximately 6:30 p.m. or prior to adjournment, whichever occurred earlier,
  which had been standard practice prior to the COVID-19 pandemic; and expressed her
  appreciation for the community’s patience and understanding as adjustments to meeting
  protocols are made as needed.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Vice Mayor Carroll led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  INVOCATION

  Rabbi Richard Steinberg from Congregation Shir Ha-Ma’alot in Irvine provided the
  invocation.

  1.  PRESENTATIONS

  1.1  Presentation by the Greater Irvine Chamber of Commerce

  Mayor Shea introduced President/Chief Executive Officer Bryan Starr,
  Greater Irvine Chamber of Commerce, who provided an update on the
  support and resources available to the business community during the
  COVID-19 pandemic.

  Councilmember Fox suggested the creation of a task force or program on
  how the City, in conjunction with the Chamber, could provide additional
  support to local businesses.

  By consensus, the presentation was received and filed. No action was
  taken.

  INTERIM CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  There was no report.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  Councilmember Khan, as the City’s representative to the Orange County Mosquito and
  Vector Control District (District), presented a video produced by the District related to
  mosquito control.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  2
 City Council Minutes  October 27, 2020

  Mayor Shea made the following announcements:

  •  Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the Irvine Police Department, in partnership with the
  Greater Irvine Chamber of Commerce, will be hosting a Trick-or-Treat Drive-thru
  event at the Orange County Great Park on Friday, October 30 from 6 p.m. to 9 p.m.
  This is a free event and will feature candy and other giveaways, Halloween
  decorations, police vehicles, and the wonderful men and women of the Irvine Police
  Department. Participants are reminded to wear their costumes, and face covers, and
  to remain in their vehicles at all times.

  •  The community is invited to the 38th Annual Holiday Faire on Saturday, November 7.
  During this one-day outdoor shopping event, local artists will showcase unique
  handmade gifts for purchase. This year’s Holiday Faire is being held entirely outdoors
  at the Orange County Great Park's Palm Court with advance tickets required to offer
  vendors and visitors more space to socially distance and shop safely, with new safety
  protocols in place. Tickets are available at yourirvine.org. Admission is $2 and tickets
  for anyone age 12 or younger are free. For more information, visit
  cityofirvine.org/holidayfaire or call 949-724-6880.

  •  Vote-by-mail ballots for the November 3 Presidential General Election have been
  mailed to all registered voters in Orange County, and early voting is underway. Voters
  can cast their ballot one of three ways: 1) U.S. Mail (no stamp is required); 2) Via
  any official Ballot Drop Box location in Orange County, including ten locations in
  Irvine; and 3) Beginning Friday, October 30, at any Vote Center in Orange County,
  where voters can also register to vote, request a replacement ballot, get help in
  multiple languages, and vote with an accessible voting machine at any Vote
  Center. Vote Centers will be open October 30 through November 2 from 8 a.m. to 8
  p.m. and November 3 from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. There will be 14 Vote Centers in Irvine,
  including the Irvine Civic Center. For more information, visit cityofirvine.org/election
  or call the City of Irvine Election Hotline at 949-724-6159.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  3
 City Council Minutes  October 27, 2020

  •  The Regional Housing Needs Allocation (RHNA) is the number of homes that a City
  has to plan for in its General Plan Housing Element, mandated by the State of
  California and released every eight years. The state requires a City to find adequate
  sites for both the total number of homes and a number of homes across all income
  categories. If a City is unable to find adequate sites to accommodate the RHNA, it
  may become ineligible for millions of dollars in state funding. The City has been very
  involved throughout this process over the last year, expressing concern with the final
  RHNA methodology. In September, the City of Irvine received a draft RHNA
  allocation of 23,554 housing units, and an appeal of the RHNA allocation was filed
  on October 26, which challenges the number assigned to Irvine based on: 1)
  Inaccurate assumptions regarding transit, protected open space, and wildfire danger;
  2) Unfair redistribution of units from other Cities; 3) The methodology violates state
  law; and 4) A change in circumstances due to COVID-19. RHNA appeal hearings will
  be held in December and January, and Final RHNA allocations will be released in
  February 2021. Updates will be provided on RHNA in the coming months.

  •  The Greater Irvine Chamber of Commerce held its Celebrate Resilience awards
  program and the City Council was honored with the Community Impact Award. This
  award recognizes those who have made significant contributions to help the
  community face or overcome challenges presented by the coronavirus pandemic.
  The City Council is proud of the work the City has done since the pandemic began to
  keep its residents and businesses safe.

  •  After six years as City Clerk and a 22-year career in public service, Molly Perry will
  be retiring on December 30. Molly was appointed City Clerk in 2014 after serving as
  City Clerk at Rancho Santa Margarita for six and a half years. From 2005 to 2007,
  Molly served as the first Orange County Great Park Clerk of the Board, and dedicated
  more than 16 years of service to the City of Irvine as she first joined the City in 1998.
  During Molly’s tenure, she has encouraged an increased focus on technology
  platforms resulting in increased efficiency and economic service delivery within the
  City Clerk’s Office while maintain outstanding customer service. She also served as
  the Region 10 Director of the California City Clerk’s Association, as a voting member
  of the Orange County Election Working Group, and currently serves on the National
  Board of Directors of Trauma Intervention Programs, Inc., a local non-profit. In 2013,
  Molly was awarded the “City Clerk of the Year Award” and a “2013 Honorable Mention
  in Public Relations,” by the Southern California City Clerk’s Association.

  ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS

  There were no additions or deletions to the agenda.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  4
